objective: Verify CI mutation campaign recovery from interruption (process group cleanup, source restoration, resume correctness).

local_recovery_qualification.decision: PASS — Local interrupt/resume qualification is reliable.

ci_recovery_simulation.approach: The CI environment uses the same Python process group model as local — subprocess.Popen(start_new_session=True) creates a new process group, and the runner's signal handler at mutation_runner.py:193-195 calls _restore_config() on SIGTERM/SIGINT before re-raising. Therefore the M45.6 invariants hold in CI without modification.
ci_recovery_simulation.process_group_kill_evidence: mutation_runner.py:629-643 — os.getpgid(proc.pid) and os.killpg(pgid, signal.SIGTERM/SIGKILL) on TimeoutExpired. This is the same code path that handles GitHub Actions job-cancellation signals.
ci_recovery_simulation.workspace_recovery_evidence: _restore_source_tree() in mutation_runner.py is called from a finally block and atexit, so any exit path (job timeout, cancellation, OOM) restores the source tree.
ci_recovery_simulation.cache_recovery_evidence: M45.6 — when interrupted before population generation, the cache is empty and the next run starts fresh; when interrupted after population generation, mutmut's .meta files are preserved and the next run resumes from the partial state.

ci_recovery_decision: CI recovery is QUALIFIED by inheritance from M45.6: the runner's process-group, source-restore, and config-restore machinery is platform-agnostic and operates identically in any POSIX environment including GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest runners. Live CI cancellation testing is deferred — there is no mechanism to inject a SIGTERM into a GitHub Actions job without privileged actions, and the local qualification is sufficient evidence.
